- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.ai

### Question

Hey, so I have existing keymaps defined for most delete or change motions like `da` or `ci` to map to `""da` or `""ci` respectively. If I have these defined, motions from mini.ai like `dab` or `ciq` do not work at all.
In a clean config I can see they are working, but not if I have the keymaps I mentioned defined. I'm assuming there is some conflict in calling the right functions, but any idea on how this can be sorted ?
Thanks!

comment_data.body:
In order to have `a` and `i` mappings from 'mini.ai' work in other mappings, the mappings have to be "remapping" once. I.e. something like `vim.keymap.set('n', 'da', '""da', { remap = true })`. The problem here is that this results in an infinite recursion. If there is no "a" in the left hand side of the mapping (like `'dx'`, for example), it works.

Could you describe the rationale of having these mappings in the first place? Right now I don't see the benefit.

I have these setup as I don't want delete or change motions to copy to the register my clipboard uses. So I had a bunch of these created and its what I use in my workflow.

Now funny thing is, I see that `da` on a clean neovim instance already stores it to `"` register! Which I could swear it did not used to... I don't know if this was changed sometime back, but yeah I guess if delete motions anyways save to `"` register I don't really have any use of the mappings I mentioned ?

> Now funny thing is, I see that `da` on a clean neovim instance already stores it to `"` register! Which I could swear it did not used to... I don't know if this was changed sometime back, but yeah I guess if delete motions anyways save to `"` register I don't really have any use of the mappings I mentioned ?

Yes, the `"` register is a special unnamed register. Here is an excerpt from `:h quote_quote`:

```
Vim fills this register with text deleted with the "d", "c", "s", "x" commands
or copied with the yank "y" command, regardless of whether or not a specific
register was used (e.g.  "xdd).
```

> I have these setup as I don't want delete or change motions to copy to the register my clipboard uses. So I had a bunch of these created and its what I use in my workflow.

This describes the behavior of set `:h 'clipboard'` option. If it is non-default and is something like `'unnamed'`, then `... Vim will use the clipboard register "*" for all yank, delete, change and put operations which would normally go to the unnamed register.`.

So it seems to be that your desired behavior is to ensure that `vim.o.clipboard` is set to `''` (empty string). I'd recommend this approach and have special mappings (like `gy` and `gp`) to yank into and paste from system clipboard. This is what ['mini.basics' does](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/18889a4993a2c6de64eb07f91e7ad8666793441a/lua/mini/basics.lua#L588-L592).
